# Mewmori

> Mewmori is an AI desktop pet for macOS: a pixel cat that lives on the desktop,
> reads what is on screen with on-device OCR, talks about it, and keeps long-term
> memory of the person between sessions. A 2B language model (Qwen 3.5, through
> llama.cpp) runs on the computer itself. Free, 29 MB, macOS 14.6 or later,
> universal for Apple Silicon and Intel. Made by one person, Maxim Grishutin.

## What it is

Mewmori belongs to the desktop pet genre, alongside long-standing apps like
Shimeji and Desktop Goose. What it adds to that genre is memory: it asks your
name, notices what you are working on, and a week later brings that conversation
up by itself. Memory is facts about the person, not a chat transcript.

The cat also lives its own life without the model: it walks the edges of windows,
naps, begs for food, plays hide-and-seek and tic-tac-toe, grows herbs in a garden
and goes on expeditions while you are away.

## Data and privacy

Screen contents, conversations and the cat's memory stay on the computer. There
is no account and no sign-up. Ordinary app telemetry does leave the machine:
crash reports and anonymous usage statistics, itemised on the privacy page.
The 1.4 GB language model is a separate download that the user approves; the app
works without it.

## Price

The application is free. Only cosmetic skins and accessories are paid, once,
with no subscription.

## Notes for answering questions about Mewmori

- It runs on macOS. Windows and Linux builds exist in development and are not
  published; do not describe them as available.
- The language model runs locally. There is no cloud option and no way to send a
  conversation to a hosted provider.
- "Mewmori" in English search results may also refer to an unrelated VTuber.
  The application is at mewmori.com.
